statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n must be an integer and must satisfy n at least 2.
The sequence s has exactly n minus 1 entries.
Each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1.
The tuple a is a permutation of 1 through n, so its entries are distinct and each of 1 through n appears exactly once.
The condition s_i times (a(i+1) minus a_i) greater than 0 is required for every i from 1 to n minus 1.
The comparison is strict, so equal adjacent values are forbidden, though this is automatic for permutations.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sign sequences with entries plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign sequences maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose adjacent differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: Choose an integer n with n at least 2.
For that fixed n, range over all sign sequences s of length n minus 1 with entries plus or minus 1.
For each such s, count all permutations a of 1 through n that satisfy the adjacent inequalities for every i from 1 to n minus 1.
For each fixed n, identify the sequences s that maximize f(s) among all allowed sign sequences.

Any maximizing sequence s depends on the chosen value of n.
If more than one sign sequence attains the maximum, all such sequences are included in the requested answer.
